calls.reason: The Tufts study reports 95% and 78% success on two Hanoi variants, showing useful but limited performance. Calling an entire approach merely a starting point is an evaluative judgment that this one system cannot settle.
The classification study challenges recognition efficiency, while the planning study measures reliability rather than energy use. Together they do not settle the claimed broad efficiency distinction.

Tufts reports zero success on four-block puzzles, supporting larger-task failure. But three-block success was only 34% and 0%, so the evidence is mixed on the claimed pattern of competent small-task performance followed by breakdown.
Strong vindication is an evaluative judgment. Tufts reports failures even with correct planning instructions, leaving robotic execution confounded with the reasoning failures studied by Apple.

ARC Prize reports strong Astra performance but cautions that benchmark saturation does not establish AGI. Neither that result nor the AGI Society review settles whether LLM development can lead to transformative general intelligence.

Anthropic reports broad strengths, while ARC Prize finds configuration-sensitive failures on unfamiliar games. Neither evaluates the referenced Claude Code system broadly enough to settle its undefined AGI status.
